c157.title: Students protest
c157.story: On Saturday, Anna and Max joined a student [[protest]] near the university. The city wanted to close the student library and build a parking lot. A young [[activist]] named Sofia spoke first. She said her [[activism]] started in a small library like this one. "We have one [[ideal]]: free books for everyone," she said. Max liked her [[idealism]], but he did not believe in a perfect [[utopia]]. Then workers from a local [[trade union]] arrived with big signs. They called for a [[boycott]] of the new parking company. A man in a black hat said he was an [[anarchist]] and shouted at the sky. Max's friend Oleh, a real [[cynic]], called all the politicians [[hypocrites|hypocrite]]. He said the whole march was [[nonsense]]. Two weeks later, the city kept the library open, and even Oleh brought cake.

c158.title: A debate about rights
c158.story: On Friday, Anna's class held a big debate about human rights. First, Anna talked about the history of [[feminism]]. She said her grandmother was the first [[feminist]] she ever knew. Max gave examples of [[sexism]] in sports and in job ads. Then Iryna spoke about [[homophobia]] in schools. She said every [[gay]] student should feel as safe as anyone else. Next, two students shared [[pro-choice]] and [[pro-life]] views and listened to each other politely. The history part was hard: they learned about [[antisemitism]] and [[apartheid]]. They also discussed how an [[extremist]] spreads hate online. In a short film, a young [[skinhead]] left a group of white [[supremacists|supremacist]] forever. The last topic was [[euthanasia]], and nobody agreed at all. Still, their teacher smiled: "You argued, but you respected each other."

c159.title: Left and right
c159.story: In politics class, Professor Lysenko drew two big circles on the board. One said [[communism]], and the other said [[capitalism]]. "Between them, you find [[socialism]] and many other ideas," he said. He explained that [[Marxism]] was a theory from the nineteenth century. In that theory, the [[proletariat]] were the workers in the factories. "A [[communist]] wants the state to own almost everything," he said. "A [[socialist]] wants fair taxes and free schools. A [[capitalist]] wants free markets and private business." Max told the class about his great-grandfather, a strong [[anti-communist]]. "But his neighbor called everyone [[comrade]], even the mailman," Max laughed. At the end, the professor wrote one more word: [[liberalism]]. "Next week, we argue about freedom," he said, and the class groaned happily.

c160.title: Anna's newspaper internship
c160.story: In July, Anna started a month-long internship in a busy [[newsroom]]. An older [[journalist]] named Petro showed her how to check every fact. Next to him sat a [[columnist]] who was writing the Sunday [[editorial]]. At noon, a [[correspondent]] called from abroad with an [[exclusive]]. She had proof of a big [[scandal]] at a local football club. A [[tabloid]] already had rumors about it. "They want [[publicity]], not facts," Petro said. The [[publisher]] read the morning [[digest]] and asked for a quick [[rewrite]]. He wanted the true story, not the old [[narrative]] about the club. By evening, all the [[media]] were waiting outside the club for a briefing. Petro let Anna write the headline. The next morning, the [[mass media]] everywhere repeated it.

c161.title: Anna's cousin in the army
c161.story: Anna's cousin Taras was a [[cadet]] only four years ago. Now he is an [[officer]], and he trains every new [[recruit]]. On Sunday, he visited Anna and told stories over tea. His [[lieutenant]] is strict but fair, and his [[sergeant]] tells terrible jokes. Last month, his [[battalion]] practiced moving a [[convoy]] of trucks through a [[checkpoint]]. They slept one night in a cold [[bunker]] and wore [[camouflage]] in the forest. A small [[drone]] watched them from above, and a [[tank]] moved slowly behind. In the exercise, half of the soldiers played enemy [[combatants|combatant]]. Taras was the colonel's [[adjutant]], so he carried the orders on foot. Anna asked why he chose the army. "I'm a [[patriot]], and I want my family safe," he said. Most of all, they all dream of marching in a big peace [[parade]] together.

c162.title: Who stole Max's bike?
c162.story: One morning, Max's bike was gone from the street outside his building. He called the [[cops|cop]], and a young [[detective]] named Koval came an hour later. On the street camera, they saw the [[silhouette]] of a tall man at night. Koval knew him: a local guy with a history of [[shoplifting]] and [[vandalism]]. He had an [[alibi]]: he said he was at his aunt's house all night. The next day, he came back on the [[pretext]] of walking his dog. The police stopped him and found [[ganja]] in his pocket. Koval checked his [[dossier]] and asked for a [[polygraph]] test. Before the test even started, the young [[vandal]] confessed. He and an old soccer [[hooligan]] friend took the bike as a stupid joke. Max got his bike back that evening, with a scratch and a new lock.

c163.title: A hacker on trial
c163.story: Anna's law class visited a real courtroom on Tuesday. A young [[hacker]] named Denys sat quietly next to his lawyer. He was on trial for [[hacking]] into a game company and running an email [[scam]]. He also sold [[warez]] on a [[peer-to-peer]] network, against [[copyright]] law. His [[barrister]], an older woman, worked [[pro bono]] because Denys had no money. She talked about an old [[precedent]] and showed an [[affidavit]] from his teacher. Then the [[bailiff]] asked everyone to stand. The [[tribunal]] read its [[verdict]]: guilty, but with a second chance. Now Denys must help a bank find weak spots in its apps. He even has to read every [[disclaimer]] before he clicks "I agree."

c164.title: A film about gangs
c164.story: On Friday night, Max watched an old film about the [[mafia]] with his dad. In it, an old [[gangster]] flies to Tokyo to meet the [[yakuza]]. The two groups start a long [[vendetta]] over drug [[trafficking]]. They fight about [[cannabis]] fields and boxes of [[opium]]. Behind them all is a huge crime [[syndicate]]. In the end, a police [[raid]] stops everything in one night. The police find [[bongs|bong]], a [[pistol]], and an old [[shotgun]] in the basement. An expert checks the [[caliber]] of every bullet. Max's dad fell asleep before the end, so Max had to tell him everything.

c165.title: A true-crime podcast
c165.story: Anna listens to a true-crime podcast on her way to class. This week, the host talks about a [[maniac]] from an old case. A doctor explains that he was a [[psychopath]], not just a [[sadist]]. He was also a cruel [[abuser]], and his family lived with years of [[abuse]]. Later, he began [[stalking]] young women in his town. The police finally stopped him after a failed [[kidnapping]] with [[chloroform]]. In the second part, an expert explains how to protect children from a [[pedophile]] online. She also explains why [[incest]] and other family crimes often stay hidden. Then a [[coroner]] describes her work in the city [[morgue]]. She laughs and says her hobby is [[cannibalism]] in spiders. Anna takes off her headphones and decides to listen to music tonight.

c166.title: A thriller about terror
c166.story: Anna is reading a thriller about the fight against [[terrorism]] in an imaginary country. In the book, a [[terrorist]] group plans an attack on a big port. Its leader is a [[jihadist]], and his men are [[insurgents|insurgent]] from the mountains. They join forces with a [[separatist]] army from the north. Together, they plan [[sabotage]] at the main power station. But the police find a [[detonator]] in an old car. Then they discover a whole [[arsenal]] of weapons on a farm. The [[commandant]] of the base sends soldiers and a young [[medic]]. A navy ship uses [[sonar]] to find the [[aggressors|aggressor]]' small boat. The president arrives at the port with a special [[escort]]. A police [[sniper]] watches the crowd from a roof. The attack never happens, and Anna finally falls asleep at 2 a.m.

c167.title: Max builds a computer
c167.story: Max decided to build his own [[desktop]] instead of buying one. He bought new [[hardware]] and spread it all over the kitchen table. First, he read the [[manual]] carefully, page by page. He checked every [[component]] and placed the [[processor]] very gently. He pushed extra memory into each [[slot]], a big [[upgrade]] for games. Then he tested the keyboard [[input]] and the screen [[output]] with a small program. A tiny [[buffer]] error appeared, but he fixed it in five minutes. That evening, his friend Ira brought an old [[prototype]] from her grandfather's garage. Its [[transistors|transistor]] were huge, and it could hold only one [[byte]] at a time. Max laughed: his new computer was a million times faster.

c168.title: Max learns coding
c168.story: At Max's company, a [[programmer]] named Lena offered to teach him [[coding]]. On his first day, Max wrote a simple [[test case]] for the login page. A [[tester]] ran it and then read the [[log]] with him. Next, the team started a small [[open source]] project: a friendly help [[bot]]. The bot answers any [[prompt]] about the city's buses. Soon a [[contributor]] from Lviv added a [[plug-in]] for the weather. It uses a free weather [[API]], so the bot knows when it rains. Max asked the bot, "Do I need an umbrella?" It said yes. Next week, the [[beta]] goes to real users, and Max is a little nervous.
